newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocca calls for more aid from Europe.
newsitem.headline: Morocca calls for more aid from Europe.

text.p: Morocco's finance minister on Thursday called for a boost in aid from Europe to help countries in the south Mediterranean build a prosperous zone free of violent strife.

Mohamed Kabbaj, speaking at a seminar to mark Morocco's association accord with the European Union that will take effect at the start of the year, also asked participants to fulfil promises to increase Morocco's aid under the Mediterranean programme MEDA.
Morocco currently gets about $1.5 million annually -- or $0.055 per each of its some 27 million people -- through MEDA.
Kabbaj also said the European Investment Bank had been conservative in its lending in the region, which is about 700 million ecus ($868 million) per year for all the south Mediterranean zone.
Countries in the south Mediterranean zone include Morocco, Mauritania, Algeria, Tunisia, Egypt, Jordan, Israel, Lebanon, Syria, Turkey, Malta and Cyprus.
Kabbaj also told the participants from the European Union that the body should lift trade restrictions on Morocco.

"(The EU countries) should rapidly lift all restrictions on trade, notably agriculture...Restrictions lead to a loss of global competitivity throughout the region which finds itself in total competition which the most active zones like Asia and Latin America."
Moroccan farmers have complained in particular that the EU has cut their export allocation for citrus and tomatoes, putting them at a severe disadvantage with EU member Spain.
